ruling.author: velvetmonkey
ruling.scope: PR 244 changes ONE protected artifact, test/fixtures/readme-demo-output.txt, and Ben approved that file changing on 2026-09-06 at 11:07, in answer to the question 'may test/fixtures/readme-demo-output.txt change, for PR 244?'. He answered yes. WHAT THE BRANCH DOES: `seal demo` printed a child reply that it REBUILT from the data file on disk, so the transcript asserted an event the demo had not observed. spine/proxy.cjs now forwards the child's real stdout line and the demo prints only what it saw. The recorded output must therefore move, which is why this ruling exists. WHY THIS BRANCH AND NOT PR 227: a forensic lane on a separate seat ran both demos and scored files-227-correct 0, files-244-correct 3; PR 227 still carries childReplyFromDataFile(dataFile), which reconstructs the very line the fix exists to stop reconstructing. PR 227 is closed with that evidence. THREE CONCERNS I RAISED AGAINST THIS FIXTURE AND THEN MEASURED, all three withdrawn, recorded so they are not re-raised: (1) The fixture bakes the path /home/monkey/scratch/demoline3/work, a lane worktree. Withdrawn: the only consumer is test/readme-demo-transcript-guard.test.cjs, and scripts/readme-demo-transcript-guard.mjs line 67 rewrites every /home, /tmp and /var path to <volatile-path> before comparing, so no check ever reads it. Main's fixture already carries machine-specific paths of the same kind. (2) The demo's ASSURANCE block, 'authorization rule tested; product state and forwarding tested; client and machine trusted.', is deleted from spine/demo.cjs. Withdrawn: it is a declared retirement under the standing rule 'proven means strict' of 2026-08-27, and test/authorization-status-surfaces.test.cjs locks its ABSENCE with a physical tamper control that goes red when the sentence is re-added. (3) The transcript guard's replay assertion changed from requiring already_consumed to requiring verdict BLOCK, which looked like a weakened assertion. Withdrawn: test/spine-retry.test.cjs line 209 asserts the demo output must NOT contain already_consumed, because that reason string was reconstructed rather than observed. The load-bearing property, that the replay did not run the call again, is still asserted by name through 'child calls observed: still 1'. MECHANICS: the branch was brought up to date with `gh pr update-branch --rebase` BEFORE this ruling was written, so the merge base is current main d8f5198b and exactly one protected file is reported. Contrast the PR 252 ruling it retires, which had to enumerate five byte-identical files because a merge commit already existed.
retires: The 2026-09-06 ruling from PR 252, base c5c01c064c96ad87b18caa6438522f75e69048b6, which merged to main as 6c79c9fd5debdee83a8d4bcebbb2b3017ca27c8c and no longer applies to any open change.
